CLAUDE.md

Source: CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

What this is

zupix reads and writes PNG, JPEG, WebP and QOI with every codec compiled into the package. It decodes to a nativeRaster, a double array or an integer array with a bits attribute, encodes from the same shapes, and reads header and metadata (size, depth, ICC and EXIF bytes, orientation) without decoding pixels. R users call the pix_ functions; sibling packages call the same codecs from C through a registered table. It has no Imports, no LinkingTo and no SystemRequirements: zlib comes from R’s own toolchain and everything else is vendored. It does not manage colour (that is zucolor), process images (zuvips, magick), read tiled or pyramidal images (zuvips), or draw (zuraster). TIFF arrives in v0.2.0; GIF, AVIF and JPEG XL are later still.

The specification is .agents/design.md, adopted from RFC 0055. It outranks this file: CLAUDE.md orients, the design doc decides. Its decisions (§13) are all still marked (C), and its open questions (§15) are open.

Current state

Scaffolded 2026-10-30 with create-pkg.sh; no functionality yet. The roadmap in .agents/roadmap.md takes it to v0.1.0. DESCRIPTION’s Title and Description are still the scaffold’s placeholders.

Stage tracking

Progress toward the next version is tracked as GitHub sub-issues, so the parent issue shows a progress bar such as “6 of 7”.

  • One parent issue per target version, titled with the bare version, for example v0.1.0. v0.1.0 issue: created by pkg-roadmap.
  • One sub-issue per roadmap stage, titled as the roadmap titles it, for example Stage 3 — R interface, and linking to that section. The number of stages is whatever the roadmap has; there is no fixed scale.
  • Every tracking issue carries the stage label, so it can be told apart from bug and feature issues and left out of open-issue counts.
  • Close a stage by merging its pull request. Put Closes #<n> in the body of the stage’s pull request. Never close a stage whose exit criteria are not met; record a deviation in the roadmap first.
  • The roadmap stays authoritative. The issues record which stages are done, not what a stage requires. Adding, removing or renaming a stage means editing the roadmap and the sub-issues in the same change.
  • Each stage has a CI tier, quick or full. The roadmap sets it, and quick is the default. See Continuous integration for what each means. The second-to-last stage, Full CI, runs the full set and fixes what it finds before v0.1.0 readiness.
  • Close the parent issue when CRAN accepts the version and it is tagged. Opening a parent issue implies at least one stage sub-issue; a parent with no sub-issues shows no progress on the board.

Versioning

A new package develops at 0.0.0.9000 and targets 0.1.0 for its first CRAN release. Set Version: 0.1.0 and the matching NEWS.md heading when the package enters Pre-flight. Bump to 0.1.0.9000 only after CRAN accepts it, never before: a .9000 version above an unreleased 0.1.0 heading is wrong.

Until the first release the R API may change freely. Sibling packages can still depend on this one before CRAN does, through Remotes: or LinkingTo:. The design plans these: zuraster (Imports and LinkingTo, the C table), zuocr (Imports, R level), and zupdf and zuvips (Suggests); zusvg may move its PNG output to the table. A change to the C API in inst/include/zupix.h or zupix-r.h, or to the pixel shapes of design §6.2 (the imaging stack’s contract), breaks them even before 0.1.0. A package that others wait on should reach CRAN first.

Commands

Run from the package root.

Rscript -e 'devtools::load_all()'                # compile src/ and load
Rscript -e 'devtools::document()'                # roxygen -> NAMESPACE, man/
Rscript -e 'devtools::test()'                    # full testthat suite
Rscript -e 'devtools::test(filter = "<name>")'   # one test file
Rscript -e 'devtools::test(shuffle = TRUE)'      # order independence
Rscript -e 'devtools::check()'                   # R CMD check
air format .                                     # format R sources

Occasional, for vendored code and its gates:

tools/vendor/verify          # vendored tree == manifest + patches (offline)
tools/vendor/fetch [source]  # re-vendor from tools/vendor/manifest.tsv
tools/check-symbols          # zupix.so imports no stdio/exit/abort/getenv/RNG,
                             # exports only R_init_zupix (add --canary)
tools/run-benchmarks         # design §10, into .agents/benchmarks.md

Architecture

Growing as stages land; .agents/design.md §4 plans the layers.

  • src/vendor/<lib>/ is upstream code, trimmed by tools/vendor/<lib>.files, pinned and patched by tools/vendor/manifest.tsv and tools/patches/<lib>/. Never edit it by hand: change a patch and re-run tools/vendor/fetch.
  • Wuffs and qoi.h are single files compiled through one zupix translation unit each (src/zpx_wuffs.c, src/zpx_qoi.c), which set the module and implementation macros. libjpeg-turbo and libwebp compile file by file from the object lists in src/Makevars.
  • src/jpeg-config/ holds zupix’s hand-written stand-ins for the headers libjpeg-turbo’s CMake build generates.
  • The core (src/zpx_core.h and the zpx_*.c it declares) includes no R header. zpx_decode.c sees only Wuffs’s declarations and calls each format’s decoder functions directly: Wuffs’s generic wuffs_base__image_decoder trips clang’s -fsanitize=function.
  • src/zpx_scan.c holds zupix’s own container scanners (PNG chunks, JPEG markers, RIFF chunks, QOI header, EXIF IFD0), the package’s only hand-written parsers of untrusted input (D12). Every read is preceded by a length check against the bytes left; keep it that way, and add a hostile case to the tests for each new field.
  • Test fixtures for JPEG and WebP are generated by tools/make-fixtures.R (needs the jpeg and webp packages); PNG and QOI are built byte by byte in tests/testthat/helper-images.R, which also splices metadata into files.
  • The C table (src/zpx_table.c) is the public C API: inst/include/zupix.h (pure C99, also the source of the core’s shared types) and inst/include/zupix-r.h. tools/zupixtest calls it from outside, run by abi.yaml on all three OSes. tools/zupixtest is .Rbuildignored.
  • src/zpx_r.c is the only R-aware C; src/zpx_init.c registers it. It returns pixels or a zupix_failure list, and R/conditions.R turns the failure into the classed condition, so no C code raises an R error.
  • Decoding is two-phase: probe (header, limits on declared sizes), then allocate (R vectors only, so an R error leaks nothing), then decode. Array outputs go through a row-major RGBA intermediate that is counted in max_bytes; an 8-bit nativeRaster decodes in place.
  • Wuffs v0.4.0-alpha.12 decodes still WebP only, and fails on a VP8L bitstream inside a VP8X container. zpx_decode.c hands it a rebuilt simple-format file for both an animated file’s first frame and an extended VP8L file (zpx_meta.webp_rebuild). Revisit when Wuffs is bumped.
  • Encoders write to a zpx_write_fn sink. From R the sink is a growable malloc buffer (zpx_sink.c), copied into a raw vector under R_ExecWithCleanup(), which frees the buffer even if that allocation raises an R error. Keep that pattern for any C-owned memory that must outlive a call into R.

Invariants that are easy to break

Fixed by the design, and still true. Each guards something the code will not show.

  • No Imports, LinkingTo or SystemRequirements. zlib is linked with -lz from R’s toolchain (D3); every other codec is vendored. A system library breaks the source install the package exists for.
  • The core (zpx_*.c) includes no R header, raises no R error and never longjmps out of itself; it returns a zpx_status. Fuzz targets link it without R, and consumers call the table from inside vendored libraries’ frames (design §4, §7), where an R error would unwind through foreign code. Only zpx_r.c touches R objects.
  • Check limits on declared sizes before allocating (design §6.5, D7), and fail with zupix_decode_error when the scanner’s and Wuffs’s sizes disagree. Otherwise a small file declaring a huge image allocates gigabytes, or passes the limits with one size and decodes with another.
  • Return the pixels the file holds. ICC profiles and colour chunks are returned or reported, never applied (D8); EXIF orientation is applied only on request (D9); channels may be added, never removed (D10). Each of these is a colour decision that belongs to the caller or to zucolor.
  • zupix.h and zupix_api_v1 are an ABI. Siblings link against them before CRAN does. Never reorder or retype a field or enum value; add fields only at the end of a struct (callers set struct_size), and anything else means ZUPIX_ABI_VERSION 2 and a new table type, with zupix_get_api(1) kept working. test-abi.R and abi.yaml guard it.
  • Only R_init_zupix is exported from the shared object. No wuffs_, jpeg_, jinit, WebP or qoi_ symbol may leak, or zupix collides with any other package that links those libraries; test-abi.R checks the symbol table (design §9).
  • Decoders and encoders come from different code (D2): Wuffs decodes, while zupix’s own PNG writer, libjpeg-turbo’s compressor, libwebp’s encoder and qoi.h encode. Don’t pull a vendored library’s decoder in for convenience; hostile input goes only through Wuffs.

Testing conventions

  • Self-sufficient. Every test builds its own inputs inside the test_that() block. No file-scope objects.
  • Self-contained. Global state goes through withr::local_*(), randomised input through withr::local_seed(). Tests write only under tempdir().
  • Assert on condition classes, never message text. Use expect_error(..., class = "<pkg>_<kind>_error"). Wording belongs in snapshot tests.
  • Order independence. devtools::test(shuffle = TRUE) is part of the definition of done.
  • Borrow a conformance suite before writing one. Mainstream implementations in Python, Java, Go or Node usually ship a test corpus. Use it as an oracle rather than inventing cases by hand. The design names PngSuite, libjpeg-turbo’s testimages, libwebp’s test files and the QOI test images, with png, jpeg, webp and qoi as differential oracles (design §9). Their licences are not yet read (Q6); files that may not be redistributed are downloaded in CI only.
  • Helpers live in tests/testthat/helper-*.R. None yet.
  • Keep the suite inside the CRAN time budget. No suite yet.

Definition of done

devtools::document() and devtools::check() clean, meaning 0 errors, 0 warnings and 0 notes. The one allowed note is “New submission” before the first release. devtools::test(shuffle = TRUE) green. CI green at the change’s tier: the quick profile for a quick roadmap stage or an ordinary pull request, the full profile for a full stage, Full CI, and every release. A user-facing change also needs a test, roxygen documentation and a NEWS.md entry.

Releasing to CRAN

  • CI is the pre-submission check. The pedrobtz/r-actions R CMD check runs --as-cran on the CRAN-like runners and containers, and it replaces win-builder, the macOS builder and R-hub. None of them is a release step, and cran-comments.md lists the CI legs as its test environments.
  • Entering Pre-flight. The roadmap’s feature stages are done, the version is set as in Versioning, NEWS.md and cran-comments.md are written, and CI is green. Only submission work remains.
  • Before submitting, run pkg-critical-review once the roadmap is implemented and fix what it files, then pkg-cran-review, and resolve every finding. Both skills are in pedrobtz/r-skills.
  • The pretest is automated and does not read cran-comments.md. A NOTE that is explained but not fixed gets the upload archived. Fix the NOTE, as under Vendored native code, instead of justifying it.
  • After acceptance, pkg-post-cran tags the submitted commit with the bare version, 0.1.0 (no v), publishes the GitHub release, bumps to 0.1.0.9000, closes the version’s parent issue and moves the board card.

Editing rules

  • roxygen comments are the source. Never edit man/ or NAMESPACE by hand.
  • Edit README.Rmd, not the generated README.md.
  • Keep prose simple and short. One idea per sentence.
  • Wrap roxygen text at 80 characters and run air format . on R sources.
  • Use lower_snake_case, and prefix internal native symbols with <pkg>_.
  • Keep hard runtime dependencies at zero unless a recorded design decision says otherwise.
  • Export and document public functions. Do not create roxygen topics for internal ones.

Continuous integration

Workflows come from pedrobtz/r-actions. Call those reusable workflows instead of writing bespoke ones, and pin a released tag rather than main. Pin a workflow that holds a write token, such as coverage.yml, to a commit, with the tag in a comment. The R-CMD-check workflow must call r-cmd-check.yml, because a hand-rolled one does not count as the pre-submission check. This package calls r-cmd-check.yml@v1 and coverage.yml@v1; pkgdown.yaml is a standalone r-lib workflow.

Small edits get a small run. The shared workflows look at the files a pull request changes, compared with its merge base:

  • Markdown only, such as README.md, NEWS.md or cran-comments.md, skips every check. Only coverage and the pkgdown site run.
  • DESCRIPTION or README.Rmd as well, and nothing else, adds one R CMD check on Ubuntu R-release.
  • Any other file runs everything.

So put a README or DESCRIPTION touch-up in its own pull request. Once a pull request changes code, every later push to it runs every workflow.

Quick by default, full by exception

The full profile is slow. gctorture at step 20 alone has taken 36 to 107 minutes on sibling packages. Waiting on it between roadmap stages was the main thing slowing roadmaps down, so:

  • Pull requests run the quick profile. It should finish in under five minutes. If it doesn’t, raise gctorture’s quick-step or trim quick-containers in the caller workflows; never cut the full profile.
  • A full roadmap stage takes the full-ci label and merges only on a green full run. The roadmap gives the reason in the stage’s **CI.** line, for example first compiled code, a PROTECT or finalizer change, a vendored library, or a Windows-only path.
  • Don’t wait on the full run a merge starts on the default branch, and cancel older full runs it supersedes. A failure that only the full set shows goes on the Full CI stage issue as a comment with the run link, and is fixed there. A failure the quick profile also shows is fixed now.
  • Full CI and v0.1.0 readiness wait for a green full run on their merge commit, and the release commit always needs one.
  • Locally, run gctorture(TRUE) on the code a C change touches when it is cheap; the full run is the authority.

Vendored native code

The design plans four upstreams, none vendored yet: Wuffs (MIT and Apache-2.0, both apply; decoders for all four formats), the compression half of libjpeg-turbo 3.2.x (IJG and BSD-3-Clause), the libwebp 1.6.0 encoder (BSD-3-Clause and its PATENTS grant), and qoi.h (MIT, no tags, pinned by commit). Stage 0 records tags, commits, checksums and patches when it vendors them. Wuffs’s JPEG, WebP and QOI decoders exist only in its v0.4.0-alpha series, so D1 departs from the stable-release rule below; that is the decision the design flags for a second look.

  • Pin a stable upstream release, never master or a release candidate.
  • Record the tag, the commit and the checksums, and write down the update procedure so the next bump is mechanical.
  • Keep upstream LICENSE and NOTICE under src/vendor/<lib>/, declare the vendored code in DESCRIPTION and inst/COPYRIGHTS.
  • Keep the vendor tree clearly separated from first-party source, and record every local patch and why it exists.
  • CRAN’s compiled-code check applies to vendored code too. No stdout or stderr, no printf, abort, exit or system RNG may be linked, even behind a debug switch that never runs. Remove them with a patch in tools/patches/, list it in src/vendor/PROVENANCE, and make the vendor-verify script check “upstream plus exactly these patches”. Avoid diagnostic-suppressing pragmas too, because they draw their own NOTE. zuhtml is the reference: tools/patches/0002-no-stdio.patch and tools/verify-vendor. zuxml’s first upload was archived because it justified such a symbol instead of patching it.
  • Guard against regressions in CI: run nm -u on the built objects and fail on any of those symbols, so an upstream bump cannot bring them back.

Commits and pull requests

Short, imperative, sentence-case commit subjects, optionally scoped. Keep each commit focused and do not sweep in unrelated files. A pull request explains the user-visible outcome and the rationale, links related issues, lists the checks that were run and the tests that were skipped, and flags platform-sensitive or vendored changes. Performance claims need evidence.

Never commit or push to the default branch. Work on a branch, open a pull request, and leave it for review. Do not merge a pull request unless you are told to.

When you find a defect, in this package or in an upstream tool, open an issue for it rather than only working around it.

Working with skills

The portfolio’s workflow skills live in pedrobtz/r-skills (pkg-init, pkg-roadmap, pkg-implement, pkg-critical-review, pkg-cran-review, pkg-post-cran, pkg-readme); the general process skills are Superpowers. building-a-package.md in pedrobtz/packages walks through them in order. Both sets defer to this file where they overlap, so the settlements are recorded here.

  • One design. The specification is .agents/design.md, adopted from the package’s RFC in pedrobtz/packages/rfcs. A package with an adopted design is past brainstorming; a design change goes through the RFC, not a new spec. Superpowers’ default docs/superpowers/specs/ is not used.
  • Plans at two levels. .agents/roadmap.md holds the stages, one mergeable pull request each, with exit criteria and a CI tier (pkg-roadmap). Inside a stage, writing-plans breaks the work into tasks of one test cycle each, saved as .agents/plans/stage-<n>.md. The roadmap stays authoritative; a plan is scratch and is not kept in sync.
  • Build and merge. pkg-implement runs the stage loop: branch stage-<n>-<slug> from the stage issue, implement the plan with test-driven-development (Rscript -e 'devtools::test(filter = "<name>")' is the red/green command), open the pull request, merge on green at the stage’s CI tier. The confirmation the user gives at the start of that loop is the “told to merge” that Commits and pull requests requires, so the finishing-a-development-branch menu is not presented for stage pull requests. Any other pull request still waits for review.
  • Failures and claims. A failing check or test goes through systematic-debugging before a fix. “Green”, “done” and “ready for CRAN” are claimed only after verification-before-completion: run the command, read the output.
  • Review. requesting-code-review gates tasks inside a stage. pkg-critical-review reviews the whole package once the roadmap is implemented, with Posit’s reviewers, and files issues. CRAN’s reviewer email and GitHub review threads go through receiving-code-review.
  • Keep scratch out of the tarball. R CMD build reads .Rbuildignore, not .gitignore. It must list ^\.agents$, ^\.superpowers$ (the Superpowers task ledger), ^\.worktrees$ (if git worktrees are kept in the package directory; a sibling directory avoids the question), ^\.claude$, ^CLAUDE\.md$, ^AGENTS\.md$, ^CRAN-SUBMISSION$ and ^cran-comments\.md$. A stray top-level file is a NOTE, and the pretest archives on NOTEs.
